name: Saurians
background:
Saurians are an ancient coalition of humanoid reptiles led by giant Frog-Mages. They fight alongside a variety of powerful dinosaur-like creatures from the jungles of their native plane. 

The Saurians put their faith in the prophecies of the Frog-Mages, who believed that they would confront Havoc in order to save their world. With the opening of the Rift, however, it appears that they have returned too late. Now, they must confront the apparent failure of the ruling Frog-Mages and their prophecy.
backgroundFull:
The Frog-Mages claim that they came into being in a time long before any other species arrived in Tyria. They grew wise and powerful with the use of magical waters, developing powerful magic. They found themselves amongst unthinking creatures, and so they began to share their knowledge with the surrounding animals. Soon, these animals changed in body and mind, becoming intelligent and learning to walk and use tools, and they came to revere the Frog-Mages as their gods. 

The Frog-Mages’ skill in magic soon drew the eyes of the Havoc Gods, who sought their power. A long war ensued between the Saurians and the Daemons of the Havoc Gods, which soon became locked in a stalemate without a clear path in sight. 

The Frog-Mages turned to prophecy to divine a path for their people. They told their people three Great Prophecies: Without the Saurians, the world would burn. Without them, the world would heal. Without them, the world would break.

Without a means to overcome the Daemons, the Saurians opened Voidgates and retreated into a plane where they could be safe from them. They entered into a long hibernation and rested while the Havoc Gods ransacked and burnt their plane. They hoped that when they awoke to return, their home would have healed, and once they returned, their presence would ensure that the world could not break so long as they remained there. 

Now the re-awakened Saurians have begun to arrive in Tyria. They have learnt about the release of the Havoc Gods and the Rift with much sorrow. Some Saurians believe that it is a sign that the Frog-Mages failed in their plan to forestall the third part of the prophecy, and that the victory of Havoc is now inevitable. Others fear that some greater threat still lurks in the future, which the Frog-Mages hope to prevent. 

Uncertainty is a strange sentiment for the Saurians and their Frog-Mages, but they are not unprepared. Skilled warriors with a proud tradition of fighting Havoc, the Saurians are ready to face whatever dangers Tyria holds for them, even if it means their ultimate doom. 

How will you face your destiny?

product.description: Though their role may be less glorious than that of the Saurians making up the core of the lines, Geckos serve a no less vital role as skirmishers. The Geckos’ small frames move through difficult terrain with ease, allowing them to skirmish and fill any gaps in the line as their larger comrades’ advance. Geckos often fight from a distance, striking from dense foliage and using blowpipes and javelins to harry approaching formations or pick off isolated scouts. Others fight with sharpened clubs, making up for their relative lack of strength with precision strikes.

When the Frog-Mages set out to war, Saurian Warriors often make up the bulk of their formation. Warriors are typically not professional soldiers but rather receive their training through communal sporting events and in hunting parties. Usually, they are called up to assist in defending their home or to join in a mission ordained by a Frog-Mage. Saurian Warriors fight fearlessly because they believe that the outcome of the battle has already been determined by fate and their duty is only to carry out their part in the pre-ordained battle honourably, whether it ends in death or victory.

Deinonychuses are said to have been bred by the Frog-Mages of the Snowfeather Conclave among the frigid peaks of southern Xurasika. These feathered beasts are now highly sought after by Saurians everywhere, particularly among the Cold Stone pyramids which prize their agility and manoeuvrability over their larger Raptor cousins. It is a particular honour among Geckos to be chosen as a Deinonychus Rider, as the creatures’ feathers are considered a status symbol.

Standing at the doors of the most sacred chambers of the Frog-Mages, one may see the resplendent armour of Saurian Guardians. They are the last line of defence and the spear tip of its assaults. Guardians are elite warriors chosen from the mightiest of the Saurians.

A popular legend claims that the Chameleons were born of the Frog-Mages’ earliest attempts to create Geckos. Though cast out by arrogant Frog-Mages as failed experiments, these first Chameleons remained loyal to the Frog Mages. In return for their loyalty, the gods rewarded them for this loyalty with scales of shifting colour, allowing them to hide in plain sight.
The Frog-Mages deny they ever made such a mistake, but among Chameleons, the story remains popular nonetheless.

Slithering alongside the advancing ranks of a Saurian Contingent, snakes are a common sight. Snake Swarms move through narrow openings and across uneven surfaces, reforming when the way is clear to bite at the ankles of unsuspecting foes from beneath thick jungle foliage or gaps in ancient ruins. The Snake Swarms are difficult for enemies to get rid of due to their writhing mass and sheer numbers, making them very useful for slowing enemies.

As adaptable and varied as the Geckos they are chosen from, Gecko Chiefs guide their people through times of war. Often, they are appointed by a council of Priests based on their valour, either for the deeds which they have already performed or those which they are prophesied to one day do. The chosen Gecko is offered a sacred skull worn by their predecessor. If the wearer falls honourably in battle, a new feather will be added to the mask in their memory.

Flying majestically above the jungles and mountains of Xurasika, Pterodactyls are a common sight. In ancient days, it is said that the Frog-Mages would use these creatures as sentries to warn of intruders. Geckos eventually took this further, learning how to ride atop their backs. Now, Pterodactyl Riders are a vital part of Gecko society, typically chosen by Gecko Priests and occasionally Frog-Mages. Being chosen as the caretaker of a Pterodactyl is a great honour. Riders fill a number of roles, ranging from transporting goods and information between remote outposts to surveying lands.

Legends say Ripjawdactyls were first bred from the most aggressive Pterodactyls by the Frog-Mages during the War of Fate. Those familiar with the species can easily pick them out from their more docile relatives by their low-sloping heads and the sharpened ridges on their beaks, which allow them to tear away at the flesh of their prey. They have a well-earned reputation for aggression, often sporting scars on their wings from fights among the other Ripjawdactyls over pecking order. On the battlefield, they rely on their weight and sharpened beaks to tear at foes.

A formation of Raptor Riders sweeping into battle with lances lowered is a harrowing sight for those caught in their path. Even more horrifying is watching the Raptors tear apart those who panic and run, hunting down the freshly wounded prey. Among the animals the Saurians keep, Raptors have a reputation for predatory cunning: escaping their pens, hunting in packs, and even opening sealed doors. Their handlers often encourage these instincts, seeking to ensure their beasts are deadly and primed for war.

Gators often live among the swamps and rivers at the edge of Saurian society. As a result, some outsiders tend to view them as primitive brutes or as lacking in intelligence. Most Gators reply that the confines of pyramid corridors and strict traditions do not fit them; they prefer the simple lives of hunters in the open swamp. Saurians tend to see the Gators as clearheaded and straightforward, wise in their own way, a viewpoint often opposed to the sophisticated learning of the Gecko Priests.

A young Gecko Priest fascinated by the ancient prophecies of his people. Though his predictions have so far failed to pan out, he hopes that learning to interpret the writings left by the Frog-Mages might finally earn him a place among the other priests. While his overeager predictions and lack of confidence has led some to believe that perhaps leadership is not his destiny, Teqi is determined to prove them wrong.

Saurian Veterans wield weapons and armour forged from alloys of ancient relics, strange metals not seen since the ancient War of Fate. Veterans can draw on a vast arsenal of weapons, including great weapons tipped with Darkglass to slice through thick armour, long spears to turn an enemy’s momentum against them, and weighted clubs to batter foes. Veterans are those Saurian Guardians who have already fulfilled their duty upon the field, bringing the prophecies of the Frog-Mages into being.

Some whisper that Kikatle has inherited the gift of immortality from his Frog-Mage mentor, Lanaxi, since his death over a century ago. Though he bears many scars from his countless battles against Daemons and invaders, Kikatle has lost no strength to age or wounds while the lessons of battle have made him a canny leader and tactician. It is said that the legendary Frog-Mage Lanaxi foresaw that the unity of the Saurians could only be achieved through his own self-sacrifice and personally tasked Kikatle with seeing that his goals were carried out.

Gator Veterans pulverize their foes with heavy clubs forged by the most skilled crafters in the Pyramid. They proudly wear their shining armour marked with their deeds, both accomplished and prophesised by the Frog-Mages. Their people’s culture demands that they lead by example: the first to enter battle and the last to leave it.

product.description: Born from the same egg, the twins Hana and Haki have always shared a close bond; even their naming prophecies are closely interlinked. Prophesied to be a veil of protection for his sister, the gentle but dutiful Haki has long taken on something akin to a big brother role while serving as his sister’s eyes and ears in battle. Hana, while typically shy and sweet, becomes coldly analytical in battle, picking off enemies with poison darts with the precision of a sniper. Her keen eye and steady hand have picked off many intruders to the foggy swamplands surrounding Xaqi pyramid, eliminating threats

Dragon Lizards earned their name from their ability to spew fire. They are popular hunting companion for Geckos, who drive their intended prey towards the Dragon Lizard to enjoy a charred meal. In turn, some Gecko handlers ensure any food they prepare for their Lizards is soaked in oil to enhance the potency of their fiery breath.
Alchemists prize the glands of these creatures, which produce a highly flammable liquid when exposed to air. Even small quantities, found in the creature’s blood, can cauterise minor wounds instantly. Of course, transporting such glands has proven extremely dangerous

product.description: Frog-Mages are imposing figures, reigning over the rest of their society as semidivine figures. Saurian legends speak of a time before time when the Frog-Mages walked among the gods and wielded an immense power capable of shaping peoples and Planes to the dictates of fate. Their long slumber has left them greatly diminished; their memories are fragmented, their powers a mere shadow of what they once were, and their bodies so frail that they are confined to palanquins. Yet, even in this state, they still possess a powerful command of the arcane.

The Spiked Lizards make fearsome predators, making use of their ability to launch the hollow bone growths from the tips of their tails at arrow-like speeds to catch prey even at a distance. These often shatter on impact, launching shards of bone any creatures unfortunate enough to find themselves close to the blast. The launched bones then regrow slowly, not unlike hair, over the course of a few days or weeks.

product.description: After awakening from the long slumber in a pale and sickly state, Satloxatle has dedicated himself to reversing the damage done to him and his fellow Frog-Mages over the course of their long dormancy. After many failures through more traditional means, Satloxatle turned to alchemy and potion brewing, where he gained fame as a deadly poisoner. During this long period, he led the pyramid of Okoye into isolation, cutting off the outside world in order to dedicate himself to his craft while sending out envoys to forage or steal anything that he needed for his experiments.

A Gator veteran who places his faith in his own strength rather than in priests and prophecies. A renowned warrior among his tribe, he was assigned the duty of personally protecting Teqi. Such a position is usually seen as a high honour awarded only to the most respected veterans. Some suspect, however, that Hakatlo was chosen in order to keep him chasing Teqi’s predictions and far from the temples of Tixal where his blunt remarks had been known to cause trouble.

Once a humble dung-shovelling beast handler, Xakanu’s chance encounter with some Vinci intruders awoke a love of battle. Adorning himself in bones left as scrap by the Lizards he cared for, Xakanu leapt onto the back of a rare breed of Dragon Lizard to pursue the raiders. The resulting Qetsike Stampede left fewer than a dozen Vinci survivors and earned Xakanu acclaim within his own pyramid. Xakanu quickly set out campaigning, early hunting intruding Daemons and other foes, collecting their bones as trophies. He even shares these trophies with his beloved pet, allowing Sika to chew on  Bones.

Explorers who have sailed along the rivers of Xurasika whisper of sails that drift along until approached too closely by a vessel. Those unfortunate enough to approach will have their vessel capsized by an emerging Spinosaurus, launching the crew into the water and staining the river with blood in the wake of its feeding frenzy. A Spinosaurus is a dangerous predator on land as well; its venomous spit can weaken prey, leaving them as a ready meal when it emerges from the water.

product.description: Clearing paths as it plods forward through the thick jungle or whatever obstacles stand before it, the Triceratops serves a vital role for the Saurians both on and off the battlefield. In times of peace, Triceratops make for formidable beasts of burden, capable of transporting platforms filled with stone, food, and trade goods. These herbivores have voracious appetites which require them to eat through huge quantities of foliage. While those in Xurasika can rely upon the vast jungles of their continents, those in more isolated pyramids constantly struggle to satisfy their hunger.

Spears snap and swords sunder against the thick bone that covers the body of an Ankylosaurus. Though generally quite docile, this creature is dangerous prey because of its thick hide and dense bones. Once provoked, a strike from its mace-like tail can shatter bone and steel with ease. Some Conclaves even tip the spikes on the tails of particularly prized Ankylosauruses with Darkglass or gold to symbolise their status and increase the power of their already deadly swings.

No one seems to agree on how Dread Gators came to be. Some Saurians whisper that these beings are the spawn of some ancient Frog-Mage rite that failed, a primeval form of Gator that lacked any semblance of intelligence, or Gators who underwent dark arcane rituals to fight in the War of Fate. No matter the reason, they were prevented from entering the Long Slumber. Naturally, the Frog-Mages dismiss such claims, but if they know the true origins of these beings, they have not spoken of it.

product.description: Quetzalcoatl are not creatures found in nature but avatars of the Feathered Serpent God herself, which can be invoked into being for a time by the Frog-Mages. Their scales shimmer with a terrible beauty and they possess powerful magic which can sweep aside entire formations with a thought. Quetzalcoatls are a reflection of the Feather Serpent god’s divine fury, terrifying foes with visions of inevitable demise before the fight even begins.

product.description: Riding atop swift-footed Raptors, these Veterans follow the flow of battle closely. Few impetuous riders have survived long enough to claim the title of Veteran. They know how to wait for the right moment to strike, waiting for their foes to expose themselves before delivering the fatal blow.

gains.name: Tyrannosaur

product.description: Predators with massive jaws balanced by sweeping tails, Tyrannosaurs are said to have been shaped by the Frog-Mages themselves to be a living weapon in the War of Fate. The Tyrannosaurs’ natural ferocity was deemed so vital that their eggs were stored deep inside each pyramid during the Long Slumber. Preserved as a reminder of the catastrophic conflict that drove them into hiding, they were to be awoken only if the need was great enough.

product.description: In the confusion of battle, Deinonychus Chiefs are expected to guide the agile reptilian mounts through the thick jungle underbrush or shattered ruins of cities to where they are most needed. Easily recognised by the metal helm upon his Deinonychus or the skull on his own, the Chief arrives, bringing either reinforcements or new commands to where they are most needed in order to control the tides of war.

Leaders of the reclusive Chameleons, these Chiefs live alongside their people on the edge of Saurian territory, typically preferring to avoid the crowded Pyramid cities except in times of dire urgency. They usually view their first duty as being to their clan and fellow Chameleons. Chiefs are not ordained by fate or Priests but rather elected from among the most skilled hunters and warriors within their community. Those elected for this role, nonetheless, are an important tie between their clan and their Pyramid.

gains.name: Starseer Palanquin

product.description: It is said that Gecko Starseers have been allowed to drink the sacred waters of their pyramids. This can be a dangerous ceremony, as those unprepared for such insight have been known to go mad. This not only has given them a unique knowledge of the secrets of fate hidden within the stars but also ties them intimately to their Frog-Mage patron.

product.description: It is said that the eldest children of the Cloud Pterodactyl God still fly above the jungles of Xurasika, watching over the Saurians. Proud and aloof, it is said that their appearance in the sky foreshadows thunder and floods. Little is known of the Dread Pterodactyls except that they are bound to aid the Frog-Mages according to secret and ancient pacts dating back to the War of Fate. Thus, in times of great need, Gecko Priests climb up mountaintops to light tall beacon towers with sacred oil to summon them.

product.description: It is said that before the Long Slumber, the Behemoths served the Frog-Mages but now, their descendants wander wild as the apex predators of Xurasika’s jungles. Only a handful of these Behemoths are known to remain but their impact can be felt throughout the continent. Their mating cries are said to echo through the mountains. They shake the ground as they move through the jungle, knocking over trees and crushing anything else beneath their feet, and their dwelling places are graveyards of the massive bones left by their unfortunate prey.

product.description: Though Saurians revere Frog-Mages as supreme guides and leaders, much of the busy work of running and administering the Conclave falls upon the Gecko Priests. This often means that they serve as the glue between the diverse communities which make up the Saurians, coordinating their efforts to work as a harmonious whole. They perform various duties, ranging from naming ceremonies for newborns to organising hunting parties and setting aside land for grazing. Even among Saurian communities who have rejected the prophecies of the Frog-Mages, Geckos often continued to carry on the role of Priests.

A Saurian Standard is forged as the final symbol of a Conclave's pacts, its emblems reflecting the auguries foretold ahead of its founding by the Frog-Mages. Some are used for ceremonies or hung in places of honour. Those brought to war usually hold prophecies of martial glory, telling of both future victories and those won in times long past. They inspire those who gaze on it with the inevitability of their coming victory.

specialRules.name: Good Shot
specialRules.description: This model gets +1 to hit rolls when shooting.

specialRules.name: Vanguard
specialRules.description: After this model is deployed, it may be placed anywhere fully within 9" of its position, over 9" away from non-Vanguard enemy units.

specialRules.name: Steadfast
specialRules.description: If a unit where most models have this rule is Shaken at the beginning of the round, roll one die. On a 4+, it stops being Shaken.

specialRules.name: Sergeant
specialRules.description: This model gets AP(+1) when attacking.

specialRules.name: Precise
specialRules.description: Gets +1 to hit when attacking.

specialRules.name: Primal
specialRules.description: For each unmodified roll of 6 to hit when attacking, this model may roll +1 attack with that weapon. This rule doesn’t apply to newly generated attacks.

specialRules.name: Unique Hero
specialRules.description: Counts as having Hero, and this model may only be taken once per army.

specialRules.name: Protection Feat
specialRules.description: Once per game, when this unit takes wounds and most of its models have this rule, you may use this rule and roll one die per wound, and on a 5+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Fortified
specialRules.description: When units where most models have this rule take hits, those hits count as having AP(-1), to a min. of AP(0).

specialRules.name: Mend
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick one friendly model within 3" with Tough, and remove D3 wounds from it.

specialRules.name: Evasive
specialRules.description: Enemies get -1 to hit rolls when attacking units where most models have this rule.

specialRules.name: Counter in Melee Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Counter in melee. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Rending in Melee Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Rending in melee. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Regeneration Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Regeneration. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Primal Buff
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 nearest friendly units within 12", which gets Enhanced Primal once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Hit & Run Shooter Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Hit & Run Shooter. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Versatile Warrior Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Versatile Warrior. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Bounding
specialRules.description: When this unit is activated, you may move all models with this rule in it by up to D3+1".

specialRules.name: Enhanced Primal
specialRules.description: If this model has Primal, it gets extra attacks on successful unmodified hit results of 5-6 from Primal (instead of only on 6).

specialRules.name: Heavy Impact
specialRules.description: Counts as having Impact(X) with hits that have AP(1).

specialRules.name: Ignores Cover
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Cover.

specialRules.name: Spell Conduit
specialRules.description: Casters within 12" that are from other friendly units may cast spells as if they were in this model's position, and get +1 to casting rolls when doing so. Friendly casters may only use this rule if this unit isn't Shaken.

specialRules.name: Precision Target
specialRules.description: Once per game, during this model's activation, pick X enemy units within 18" and in line of sight of it, and place one token on them. Friendly units get +1 to hit rolls when attacking them.

specialRules.name: Precision Spotter
specialRules.description: Once per activation, pick one enemy unit within 30" and in line of sight of this model and roll one die, on a 4+ place a token on it. Friendly units may remove tokens from their target before rolling to hit to get +X to hit rolls when attacking, where X is the number of removed tokens.

specialRules.name: Spawn
specialRules.description: Once per game, when this model is activated, you may place a new unit of X fully within 6" of it.

specialRules.name: Ignores Regeneration
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Regeneration.

specialRules.name: Crossing Strike
specialRules.description: Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and attack it with this weapon as if it was shooting. This weapon may only be used in this way.

specialRules.name: Unpredictable Fighter
specialRules.description: When in melee, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead.

specialRules.name: Rapid Charge Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game moves +4" when using Charge actions. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Reliable when Shooting
specialRules.description: This model gets Reliable when shooting.

specialRules.name: Puncture
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking units where most models have Defense 2+ to Defense 3+, this weapon gets AP(+2).

specialRules.name: Shred Mark
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which friendly units gets Shred when attacking against once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Versatile Warrior
specialRules.description: When this unit is activated, pick one effect: until the end of the activation, when this unit attacks enemies for the first time each round, all models with this rule in it either get AP(+1) or get +1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: Predator
specialRules.description: For each unmodified roll of 6 to hit when attacking, this model may roll +1 attack with that weapon. This rule doesn’t apply to newly generated attacks.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Predator
specialRules.description: If this model has Predator, it gets extra attacks on successful unmodified hit results of 5-6 from Predator (instead of only on 6).

specialRules.name: AP
specialRules.description: Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits.

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: AI units within 6” use the Villain’s Qua for Morale Tests if it’s better than their own, as long as the Villain isn’t Shaken.

specialRules.name: Tough
specialRules.description: Once a model has taken as many wounds as its Tough value, it is killed (remove from play).

specialRules.name: Counter
specialRules.description: May strike first with this weapon when charged, unless this unit is Fatigued.

specialRules.name: Rending
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and for each unmodified result of 6 to hit, those hits get AP(+4).

specialRules.name: Regeneration
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 5+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Hit & Run
specialRules.description: Once per round, this model may move by up to 3" after shooting or being in melee.

specialRules.name: Hit & Run Shooter
specialRules.description: Once per round, this model may move by up to 3" after shooting.

specialRules.name: Impact
specialRules.description: When charging, before either unit attacks, roll X dice, unless this unit is Fatigued. For each 2+ the target takes 1 hit.

specialRules.name: Caster
specialRules.description: Follows same rules as heroes, picking one random spell to cast, and spending all tokens to cast it when activated. If the chosen spell can’t be cast for any reason, then the model doesn’t cast.

specialRules.name: Reliable
specialRules.description: Attacks at Quality 2+.

specialRules.name: Defense
specialRules.description: This model gets +X to Defense rolls.

specialRules.name: Shred
specialRules.description: For each unmodified result of 1 to block hits, this weapon deals 1 extra wound.

specialRules.name: Bane
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking, the target must re-roll unmodified Defense results of 6.
